power-001.question: What is the main reason SiC (silicon carbide) is advantageous over Si for high-voltage power devices?
choices: Its breakdown electric field is about 10 times that of Si
Its band gap is smaller than that of Si
Its wafers are cheaper than Si and easier to make in large diameters
power-001.explanation: SiC has a wide bandgap of about 3.3 eV and a breakdown field about ten times silicon's (about 3 MV/cm). For the same voltage rating the drift layer can be about one tenth as thick and about 100 times more heavily doped, cutting its resistance theoretically by a factor of several hundred. Its thermal conductivity is about three times silicon's, so it handles heat well, and it is spreading in EV inverters. SiC wafers remain costlier, and the move to 8-inch is still under way.

power-002.question: Which correctly describes an IGBT?
choices: A two-terminal device with only two PN junctions
A device driven by a MOS gate that achieves a low on-state voltage through conductivity modulation from bipolar operation
A thyristor turned on by light
power-002.explanation: An IGBT combines a MOSFET input with a bipolar output, adding a p+ layer on the drain side of a MOSFET-like structure. It is voltage-driven, simplifying gate drive, and when on, holes injected from the p+ layer sharply reduce drift-layer resistance (conductivity modulation), keeping on-voltage low even at 600 V to 6.5 kV ratings. It is the workhorse of EV, rail and industrial inverters, though tail current makes it unsuitable for high frequencies.

power-003.question: Which is the channel through which current flows in a GaN HEMT?
choices: A p-type inversion layer formed under the gate
A thick, heavily doped n-type layer
A two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) formed by polarization at the AlGaN/GaN interface
power-003.explanation: In a GaN HEMT, the difference in spontaneous and piezoelectric polarization at the AlGaN/GaN interface creates a dense two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) of about 10¹³ cm⁻². Because no doping is needed to supply the electrons, scattering is low and mobility reaches about 2000 cm²/V·s, combining low on-resistance with fast switching. The 2DEG exists even at 0 V gate bias, so the basic device is normally on.

power-004.question: Which correctly describes the relationship between breakdown voltage and on-resistance in silicon power MOSFETs?
choices: Breakdown voltage and on-resistance are unrelated
Raising the breakdown voltage tends to lower the on-resistance
Raising the breakdown voltage tends to raise the on-resistance
power-004.explanation: Raising breakdown voltage requires a thicker, more lightly doped drift layer, which increases its resistance. Theoretically, the on-resistance of silicon unipolar devices scales with about the 2.5th power of the voltage rating, so doubling the rating multiplies on-resistance by about 5.7 (the silicon limit). Superjunction structures and high-breakdown-field SiC and GaN are used to break this trade-off.

power-005.question: What is the main role of an inverter in power electronics?
power-005.explanation: An inverter switches power semiconductors at several kHz to tens of kHz and varies the pulse widths (PWM) to synthesize AC of any frequency and voltage from DC. It drives variable-speed motors in air conditioners and washing machines, EVs, solar power conditioners and trains, saving considerable energy by running motors only as fast as needed. Converting AC to DC is done by a converter (rectifier).

power-006.question: In power devices, which loss mainly increases when the switching frequency is raised?
power-006.explanation: Switching loss arises because voltage and current coexist during each transition; it equals energy per switching event × switching frequency, so ten times the frequency means ten times the switching loss. Conduction loss (I²R while on) does not depend on frequency. Higher frequency shrinks inductors and capacitors, so the trend is to raise frequency using SiC and GaN, whose switching losses are small.

power-007.question: Which is a characteristic of a superjunction (SJ) MOSFET?
choices: Alternating p-type and n-type pillars in the drift layer lower on-resistance while maintaining breakdown voltage
The gate oxide is made very thick to raise breakdown voltage
power-007.explanation: A superjunction structure fills the drift region with alternating p- and n-type pillars. When off, they deplete laterally so the entire region becomes depleted, sustaining high voltage even with heavily doped n-pillars; when on, current flows through those n-pillars. This brings the on-resistance of 600 V-class silicon MOSFETs to a fraction of the classical silicon limit, and such devices are widely used in power supplies and PFC circuits. Precisely balancing the p and n charge is the manufacturing key.

power-008.question: If a power device with a thermal resistance of 2 °C/W dissipates 10 W, what is the temperature rise?
power-008.explanation: Temperature rise is thermal resistance × power: 2 °C/W × 10 W = 20 °C, so at 50 °C ambient the junction reaches 70 °C. In practice the junction-to-case, case-to-heatsink and heatsink-to-air resistances are in series and are summed. Thermal resistance behaves like electrical resistance (a thermal Ohm's law), forming the basis of cooling design that keeps junction temperature within limits.

power-009.question: What is the parasitic diode that forms structurally inside a power MOSFET called?
power-009.explanation: In a power MOSFET, the p-type body tied to the source forms a pn junction with the n-type drift region, creating a parasitic diode that conducts from source to drain—the body diode. It can serve as the freewheeling path in inverters, but in silicon MOSFETs its slow reverse recovery causes losses, so fast applications add external diodes or rely on synchronous rectification.

power-010.question: What is the general term for semiconductors with a larger band gap than silicon, such as SiC and GaN?
power-010.explanation: Semiconductors with bandgaps of roughly 3 eV or more are called wide-bandgap semiconductors; SiC (about 3.3 eV) and GaN (about 3.4 eV) are the main examples. High breakdown fields and few intrinsic carriers let them operate at high temperature, suiting high-voltage, low-loss power and RF devices. Even wider-gap Ga2O3 (about 4.8 eV) and diamond (about 5.5 eV) are called ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductors.

power-011.question: What is the main role of a gate driver for power semiconductors?
choices: To receive signals from the control circuit and drive the power device's gate with the right voltage and enough current
power-011.explanation: Power device gates present large capacitances of several nF, so fast switching needs amperes of current to charge and discharge them quickly. A gate driver takes a few-mA signal from a microcontroller and delivers this drive at the proper gate voltages (e.g., +15–18 V and a negative off-bias for SiC). Many include isolation for driving high-side devices and protection that detects short circuits and shuts down quickly.

power-012.question: Why are power devices required to be 'normally off', with no current flowing at 0 V gate voltage?
choices: To avoid the danger of current flowing unintentionally when, for example, the drive circuit fails
power-012.explanation: With a normally-on device, losing or faulting the gate-drive supply turns the device on, potentially shorting the supply and causing large currents; start-up sequencing also needs care. Power circuits therefore demand normally-off devices. GaN HEMTs achieve this with a p-type GaN layer under the gate or a cascode configuration that pairs them with a low-voltage silicon MOSFET.

power-013.question: What is the main advantage of using SiC Schottky barrier diodes as freewheeling diodes in inverters and similar circuits?
choices: They are much cheaper than silicon diodes
They emit light so their state can be seen
They have almost no reverse recovery current, reducing switching loss
power-013.explanation: A Schottky barrier diode operates with majority carriers only, so it has almost none of the reverse-recovery current caused by stored minority carriers in pn diodes. Silicon Schottky diodes struggle to reach high voltages, but SiC versions are made at 600–1700 V. As freewheeling diodes in inverters and PFC circuits, they cut not only their own losses but also the turn-on losses of the complementary switch.

power-014.question: Which is a characteristic of a thyristor?
choices: Once turned on by a gate signal, it stays on until the current falls nearly to zero
It can be turned off freely at any time by a gate signal
power-014.explanation: A thyristor is a four-layer PNPN switch; a gate pulse triggers positive feedback between its PNP and NPN transistor sections, turning it on and keeping it on without further gate signal (latching). Turning it off requires dropping the current below the holding current, which happens naturally at each AC zero crossing. Handling several kV and kA, thyristors serve in HVDC transmission and high-power rectification; GTOs can also be turned off by the gate.

power-015.question: In high-power modules, what is the main purpose of the insulating substrate (such as a ceramic substrate) placed under the power chips?
choices: To electrically insulate the chips from the heat sink while conducting heat well
power-015.explanation: In power modules, chips at high voltage must be insulated from the grounded heatsink. Insulated substrates—ceramics such as silicon nitride (Si3N4), aluminum nitride (AlN) or alumina with copper bonded on both sides—block current while conducting heat well. AlN offers high thermal conductivity, while Si3N4 is mechanically strong and crack-resistant, favored in applications with severe temperature cycling such as EVs.

power-016.question: When SiC or GaN power devices switch at high speed, which problem particularly needs countermeasures?
choices: Noise (EMI) and surge voltages caused by rapid changes in voltage and current
power-016.explanation: SiC and GaN switch with extremely steep voltage and current slopes—tens to 100 V/ns—so parasitic wiring inductance produces surge voltages and current through parasitic capacitances generates electromagnetic interference (EMI). Countermeasures include short, wide interconnects to reduce inductance, gate resistors to tune switching speed, and snubbers and filters.

power-017.question: If the current in a wire with a parasitic inductance of 10 nH changes by 10 A in 10 ns, approximately what voltage is induced?
power-017.explanation: The voltage across an inductance is V = L·di/dt: 10 nH × (10 A ÷ 10 ns) = 10 V. Ten nH corresponds to only about 1 cm of wiring. Switching 100 A in tens of ns with SiC can generate surges of tens to over 100 V, threatening the device's voltage rating. Power modules therefore emphasize low-inductance layouts that place opposing current paths close together to cancel magnetic fields, and capacitors right next to the devices.

power-018.question: What is the purpose of a power factor correction (PFC) circuit used in power supplies?
choices: To shape the input current into a sine wave matching the voltage, bringing the power factor close to 1
power-018.explanation: A simple capacitor-input rectifier draws current only in pulses near the voltage peaks, dropping the power factor to about 0.5–0.7 and injecting harmonics into the grid. A PFC circuit—typically a boost converter—shapes the input current into a sine wave matching the voltage, raising the power factor above 0.95. Harmonic regulations in Japan and Europe apply to equipment above certain power levels, so PFC is built into PC power supplies, LED lighting and more.

power-019.question: What is the main advantage of using SiC power devices in electric vehicle inverters?
choices: They are always cheaper than silicon
Lower losses lead to longer driving range and smaller cooling systems
power-019.explanation: SiC devices have low on-resistance and switching losses and tolerate heat, reducing EV inverter losses. That can extend range on the same battery by several percent to about 10% and shrink cooling systems and inverters. Adoption accelerated after the 2018 Tesla Model 3, and the benefit is greatest with 800 V battery systems. The main drawback is higher cost than silicon IGBTs.

power-020.question: In an ideal step-down chopper (buck converter) with an input voltage of 12 V and a switch duty cycle of 0.25, what is the output voltage?
power-020.explanation: An ideal buck converter outputs input voltage × duty cycle: 12 V × 0.25 = 3 V. Varying the switch's on-time ratio adjusts the output, and an inductor and capacitor average it into smooth DC. Synchronous rectification, using a MOSFET instead of a diode, pushes efficiency above 90%. The low supply voltages of CPUs and memory are produced by multiphase buck converters on the motherboard.

power-021.question: Which DC-DC converter outputs a DC voltage higher than its input?
power-021.explanation: A boost converter stores energy in the inductor while the switch is on, then adds the inductor's voltage to the input when it turns off. Ideally the output is input ÷ (1 − duty cycle)—twice the input at a duty of 0.5. Applications include driving LEDs from a single battery cell, boosting solar-panel voltage, raising motor-drive voltage in hybrid cars, and PFC circuits.

power-022.question: At IGBT turn-off, what is the phenomenon called in which the current does not drop to zero immediately but trails off because of stored minority carriers?
power-022.explanation: An IGBT lowers drift resistance by injecting minority carriers (holes) when on, so at turn-off current continues until they recombine or are swept out—the tail current. Because it flows while the voltage is already high, it is a major source of turn-off loss and limits IGBT switching frequency to tens of kHz or less. Lifetime control and field-stop structures shorten it. MOSFETs have no tail current.

power-023.question: Which is a known challenge of SiC MOSFETs?
choices: Their breakdown voltage is lower than silicon's
Their band gap is smaller than silicon's
The interface between SiC and the gate oxide has many defects, so channel mobility tends to be low
power-023.explanation: SiC can be thermally oxidized to SiO2, but carbon-related defects remain at the interface, so channel mobility typically falls to only tens of cm²/V·s—far below SiC's bulk mobility of about 1000 cm²/V·s. Nitridation in nitric oxide (NO) and similar treatments have improved it. Threshold-voltage drift and long-term gate-oxide reliability also require more careful qualification than in silicon.

power-024.question: In SiC power modules operating at high temperatures, which material is sometimes used instead of solder to bond the chips?
choices: Sintered silver (a bonding material made by sintering silver nanoparticles and the like)
power-024.explanation: Conventional solders melt in the 200 °C range and fatigue under repeated hot cycling, preventing full use of SiC's high-temperature capability. Sintered silver, made by heating and pressing silver nanoparticles, bonds at around 250 °C yet the resulting silver melts at about 960 °C and conducts heat several times better than solder, so it is used in high-temperature, high-reliability modules such as those for EVs. Its high cost is a drawback.

power-025.question: What is the main advantage of raising the switching frequency of a power converter?
choices: Passive components such as inductors and capacitors can be made smaller
power-025.explanation: Raising switching frequency reduces the energy inductors and capacitors must store each cycle, so they can be smaller and supplies become compact and light; transformer size, for example, shrinks roughly in inverse proportion to frequency. Switching loss and noise rise with frequency, however, so low-loss, fast SiC and GaN devices are what make high-frequency operation practical.

power-026.question: In a power device gate drive circuit, what is the effect of increasing the gate resistance?
choices: Switching slows down; surges and noise decrease but switching loss increases
Switching speeds up, and both losses and noise decrease
It has no effect on switching
power-026.explanation: A larger gate resistor slows charging and discharging of the gate capacitance, softening voltage and current transitions; surges and noise drop, but longer transitions increase switching loss. Designers may use different resistances for turn-on and turn-off (separating the paths with diodes) or active gate driving that adapts drive strength, balancing loss against noise.

power-027.question: Which metric indicates how long a power device can withstand a short circuit, such as both upper and lower switches of an inverter turning on at once, without being destroyed?
power-027.explanation: Short-circuit withstand time is how long a device survives the large current of a shoot-through or load short—typically about 10 µs for silicon IGBTs. Protection must detect the fault and turn the device off within that time; IGBT drivers often use desaturation (DESAT) detection, sensing the rise in collector voltage. SiC MOSFETs, with small chips and low thermal capacity, often survive only a few µs and need faster protection.

power-028.question: What is the purpose of providing a short period in which both switches are off (dead time) when switching the upper and lower switches of an inverter?
choices: To prevent the upper and lower switches from turning on at the same time and short-circuiting the supply
To make the switches emit light
power-028.explanation: Switches take time to turn off, so turning one off and the other on simultaneously would briefly short the supply (shoot-through). Dead time is a period with both off to prevent this—several µs for IGBTs, tens to hundreds of ns for SiC and GaN. Too much dead time introduces output-voltage error, distorts motor current and lengthens freewheeling-diode conduction, so it is set as short as the devices allow.

power-029.question: Which is a known cause of degradation when current flows continuously through the body diode of a SiC MOSFET?
choices: Basal plane dislocations in the crystal expand into stacking faults
power-029.explanation: Forward current through a SiC body diode can, via electron-hole recombination energy, expand basal-plane dislocations in the crystal into stacking faults, raising on-voltage (bipolar degradation); stacking faults are planar defects that impede conduction. Remedies include buffer layers that convert basal-plane dislocations into another dislocation type during epitaxy, and integrating Schottky diodes so the body diode is not relied on.

power-030.question: Which is an example of an everyday product in which GaN power devices are increasingly used?
choices: The mechanical contacts of light switches
Compact, high-power chargers (AC adapters) for smartphones and similar devices
power-030.explanation: GaN power devices switch at hundreds of kHz to MHz, allowing much smaller transformers and capacitors in chargers; units of the same output can be about half the size. Low losses and heat also aid miniaturization. Starting with chargers for phones and laptops, GaN is expanding into data-center power supplies and EV on-board chargers.

power-031.question: What is the main role of power semiconductors?
choices: Switching or converting high voltages and currents to control power efficiently
power-031.explanation: Power semiconductors—diodes, MOSFETs, IGBTs, thyristors and more—efficiently control and convert large amounts of power by switching, as in motor drives and voltage conversion. Fine control of power flow underpins energy savings in air conditioners, EVs, data centers and renewable energy. Japanese companies are relatively strong in this field. Their role differs from memory, which stores data, and photodetectors, which handle light.
choiceNotes: Correct. They control and convert large amounts of power efficiently.
Storing data is the role of memory.
Converting light into electrical signals is the role of photodetectors.

power-032.question: What is the conduction loss of a power MOSFET with an on-resistance of 10 mΩ carrying 10 A?
power-032.explanation: Conduction loss is P = I²R: (10 A)² × 0.01 Ω = 1 W. Because it scales with current squared, doubling the current quadruples the loss, so at high currents small differences in on-resistance matter a lot. On-resistance also rises with temperature (about 1.5× at 100 °C), so real heating exceeds room-temperature estimates. Devices are often paralleled to reduce effective resistance.
choiceNotes: 0.1 W is I × R, which is not the formula for power.
Correct. 10² × 0.01 = 1 W.
100 W results from mis-converting the resistance unit (mΩ).

power-033.question: What is the main purpose of attaching a heat sink to a power device?
choices: To change the direction of current
To remove heat generated in the device and keep the junction temperature within its limit
power-033.explanation: Conduction and switching losses become heat in power devices. A heatsink spreads it over a large surface into the air, lowering thermal resistance along the heat path to keep the junction below its maximum rating. A rule of thumb says each 10 °C rise roughly halves lifetime, so lower temperatures directly improve reliability. High-power systems also use forced-air fans or liquid cooling.
choiceNotes: A heat sink is not a component for increasing switching speed.
Current direction is set by the circuit; the heat sink is irrelevant.
Correct. It removes heat and lowers the junction temperature.

power-034.question: How many switching devices does a typical three-phase inverter for driving a three-phase motor use?
power-034.explanation: A three-phase inverter has three legs—U, V and W—each with an upper and lower switch in series, totaling six switching devices (each with an antiparallel freewheeling diode). Each leg alternates between upper and lower switches with PWM to vary its average voltage, producing three-phase AC with 120° phase offsets. Six-in-one power modules integrating all six switches are widely used.
choiceNotes: Three would give only one switch per phase, unable to switch between positive and negative.
Correct. 3 phases × 2 switches = 6.
Two is the count for a single-phase half bridge.

power-035.question: In power circuits and the like, what is the small resistor placed in series in the current path to measure current called?
power-035.explanation: A shunt resistor is a small resistance placed in series with the current path; the voltage across it gives the current via V = IR—10 A through 2 mΩ produces 20 mV, which is then amplified. Low values keep losses small, and alloys whose resistance hardly changes with temperature (such as manganin) are used. At very high currents, lossless magnetic sensors such as Hall-effect sensors are also used.
choiceNotes: A gate resistor adjusts the switching speed of power devices.
A pull-up resistor pulls a signal line up to a high potential.
Correct. It is a small resistor for current sensing.

power-036.question: Why is a switching power supply more efficient than a linear power supply, which operates its transistor linearly?
choices: Because the transistor is used fully on or fully off, minimizing the time it sees voltage and current at once
Because its output voltage is always higher than its input
power-036.explanation: Transistor loss is voltage times current. A linear supply makes the transistor absorb the excess voltage while carrying the load current, so converting 12 V to 5 V is only about 42% efficient. A switching supply uses only the on state (almost no voltage) and off state (almost no current), losing little except during transitions, and reaches over 90% efficiency. It does require noise countermeasures.
choiceNotes: Correct. It minimizes the time voltage and current are present at once.
Switching supplies also use transistors, as switches.
Switching supplies include both step-down and step-up types.

power-037.question: What is the main advantage of the trench gate structure in power MOSFETs, in which the gate is buried in a groove etched into the silicon?
choices: Cells can be packed densely to increase channel width and lower on-resistance
power-037.explanation: In a trench-gate structure the channel forms vertically on trench sidewalls, so more cells fit per unit area than in planar designs, increasing total channel width. It also eliminates the JFET resistance between adjacent planar cells, lowering on-resistance. Trench gates dominate low-voltage silicon MOSFETs, IGBTs and recent SiC MOSFETs, but the field concentrates at the trench-bottom corners, so protective structures there are critical.
choiceNotes: The gate capacitance does not disappear; it actually tends to increase.
The breakdown voltage is set mainly by the drift layer and does not double from the structure alone.
Correct. Denser cells lower the on-resistance.

power-038.question: Which correctly describes the typical division of use between silicon MOSFETs and IGBTs?
choices: MOSFETs suit fast switching at relatively low voltages, while IGBTs suit high voltages of several hundred volts or more and large currents
IGBTs suit low voltage and small current, while MOSFETs suit high voltage and large current
Both can only be used for the same applications
power-038.explanation: Silicon MOSFETs use only majority carriers and switch fast, but on-resistance soars at high voltage, so they serve mostly below a few hundred volts, especially in low-voltage supplies. IGBTs keep on-voltage low at high voltage through conductivity modulation, suiting high-current uses above 600 V (EVs, industrial inverters, rail), though tail current slows them. SiC MOSFETs are now displacing both in the mid-to-high-voltage range.
choiceNotes: Correct. MOSFETs suit fast, low-to-medium voltage use; IGBTs suit high voltage and current.
The applications are reversed.
They are chosen according to voltage and frequency.

power-039.question: What is the main purpose of a snubber circuit in a power device switching circuit?
choices: To suppress voltage spikes (surges) and ringing that occur during switching
power-039.explanation: In fast switching, parasitic wiring inductance resonates with device capacitance, causing voltage overshoot (surge) and oscillation (ringing). Snubbers—RC networks or combinations with diodes—absorb this energy, protecting the device from overvoltage and reducing noise. The absorbed energy is dissipated as heat in the resistor, so component values are chosen to balance protection against loss.
choiceNotes: On-resistance is a device property and is not lowered by a snubber.
Correct. It suppresses surges and ringing.
A snubber is not meant to raise the switching frequency.

power-040.question: When one switch of an inverter turns on, which loss increases due to the reverse recovery of the diode in the opposite arm?
choices: The turn-on loss of the switch that turns on (the reverse recovery current is added to it)
Only the loss in the gate drive circuit
The loss in the heat sink
power-040.explanation: When a freewheeling diode switches to reverse bias, stored carriers produce reverse-recovery current. This current flows through the switch that is turning on, raising its peak current and turn-on loss, and the diode itself also dissipates recovery loss. The effect grows with voltage and current, so replacing the diode with a SiC Schottky diode, which has negligible recovery, greatly reduces the switch's turn-on loss.
choiceNotes: Correct. The reverse recovery current adds to the switch's turn-on loss.
Gate drive loss is not the main part of the increase due to reverse recovery.
A heat sink does not generate losses.

power-041.question: Among soft-switching techniques for power converters, which correctly describes ZVS (zero-voltage switching)?
choices: Keeping the switch on all the time
Turning the switch on when the voltage across it is nearly zero, reducing switching loss
power-041.explanation: ZVS uses resonance or similar techniques to bring the switch voltage near zero before turning it on. With almost no overlap of high voltage and current, turn-on loss and the loss from discharging the device's output capacitance disappear, and noise drops. It is used in LLC resonant converters and phase-shifted full bridges, improving server power-supply efficiency. Switching at zero current is ZCS.
choiceNotes: A switch that is always on cannot convert power.
Correct. Turning on at zero voltage reduces loss.
It is not a method of making the output voltage zero.

power-042.question: When a power MOSFET's gate is charged with a constant current, why does the gate voltage stay flat for a while (the Miller plateau)?
choices: Because the gate insulator temporarily breaks down
Because while the drain voltage is changing, the gate current is used to charge and discharge the gate-drain capacitance
power-042.explanation: While the drain voltage swings during switching, gate current goes into charging or discharging the gate-drain (Miller) capacitance Cgd, so the gate voltage stays nearly flat—the Miller plateau. The drain voltage transitions during this interval, so loss concentrates there. Plateau duration is roughly gate-drain charge Qgd ÷ gate current, so devices with small Qgd switch faster.
choiceNotes: The gate current keeps flowing.
It is not a breakdown of the insulator.
Correct. The current goes into charging the Miller capacitance.

power-043.question: Why is a negative gate voltage (for example, −3 to −5 V) sometimes applied to SiC MOSFETs or IGBTs in the off state?
choices: To prevent the gate voltage from being pushed up by voltage changes from the opposite switch, which could turn the device on unintentionally
power-043.explanation: In bridge circuits, the steep voltage change (dv/dt) when the opposite switch turns on can drive current through the Miller capacitance into the off device's gate, raising its voltage. If it exceeds the threshold, the device turns on falsely and shoots through. SiC MOSFETs, with low thresholds of 2–3 V and high dv/dt, are especially susceptible, so negative gate bias or Miller-clamp circuits provide margin.
choiceNotes: It is not meant to raise the switching frequency.
Correct. It prevents false (parasitic) turn-on.
On-resistance is set by the positive gate voltage and is not lowered by negative bias.

power-044.question: What maximum junction temperature (Tj max) is commonly specified for typical silicon power devices?
power-044.explanation: Silicon power devices typically have a maximum junction temperature of 150 °C or 175 °C. Beyond it, leakage current rises sharply, inviting thermal runaway, and lifetime shortens dramatically, so designs keep margin (operating around 125 °C, for example). SiC itself withstands over 300 °C, but package materials—solder, bond wires and resins—limit practical operation.
choiceNotes: About 500 °C is far too high for silicon device ratings.
About 50 °C would be exceeded even in normal operation.
Correct. 150 to 175 °C is typical.

power-045.question: When choosing power devices, why are devices with a voltage rating higher than the actual operating voltage used (derating)?
choices: To ensure reliability against switching surge voltages and failures caused by cosmic rays
power-045.explanation: Real circuits add surge voltages from parasitic inductance during switching, and at sustained high voltage, cosmic-ray neutrons can generate charge inside the device and cause sudden failure (single-event burnout), whose probability rises steeply with voltage. Designers therefore choose devices rated about 1.5× the operating voltage—650 V parts for a 400 V bus, for example—with even more margin at high altitude.
choiceNotes: Correct. Margin is kept for surges and cosmic-ray failures.
Higher-rated devices are generally more expensive.
Higher-rated devices generally have higher on-resistance.

power-046.question: When does the avalanche ruggedness of a power MOSFET become important?
choices: When no voltage is applied to the gate
When the current in an inductive load is interrupted and its energy drives the drain voltage up to breakdown
power-046.explanation: Abruptly interrupting current in an inductor releases its stored energy (½LI²), spiking the drain voltage to breakdown and driving the device into avalanche. Avalanche ruggedness is the energy the device can absorb without failure, evaluated by unclamped inductive switching (UIS) tests. It matters in applications that omit clamp circuits, such as relay and solenoid drivers and automotive loads.
choiceNotes: Cooling is not directly related to avalanche ruggedness.
Simply having no gate voltage does not cause avalanche.
Correct. Interrupting an inductive load can drive the device into avalanche.

power-047.question: What is a typical failure seen in power cycling tests, which repeatedly heat and cool power modules?
choices: Bond wire lift-off and solder layer cracking caused by differences in thermal expansion coefficients
power-047.explanation: Power modules combine materials with different thermal expansion: silicon chips (about 3 ppm/K), aluminum wires (about 23 ppm/K), solder, copper and ceramics. Repeated heating and cooling stresses their interfaces, lifting wire bonds and cracking solder layers, which raises thermal resistance. These are the main lifetime limiters, mitigated with copper wires, sintered joints and wire-free structures.
choiceNotes: Correct. Wire lift-off and solder cracking from thermal expansion mismatch.
Color change is not a failure criterion.
Oxide breakdown is not a typical power cycling failure.

power-048.question: In packages for fast-switching power devices, what is the purpose of a dedicated source terminal for the gate-drive return (Kelvin source)?
choices: To keep the voltage across the inductance of the main-current source path from affecting the gate drive
power-048.explanation: The source lead carrying main current has inductance Ls, so rapid current changes induce Ls·di/dt. If the gate-drive return shares this path, that voltage opposes the gate drive, slowing switching or causing oscillation (the common-source inductance problem). A Kelvin source is a dedicated source terminal for the driver that eliminates this effect, and four-pin packages are increasingly used to exploit the speed of SiC and GaN.
choiceNotes: It is not a terminal for increasing current.
Correct. It removes the effect of common source inductance.
It is not intended to shrink the package.

power-049.question: Which circuit uses a diode and capacitor to create a gate voltage above the supply to drive the upper (high-side) n-channel MOSFET of a half bridge?
power-049.explanation: Turning on a high-side nMOSFET needs a gate about 10 V or more above its source (the output node), which rises to the supply voltage when on. A bootstrap circuit charges a capacitor through a diode while the low-side switch is on and the output sits near ground, then stacks that voltage on top of the output node to drive the gate. It is cheap and simple, but the high-side switch cannot be held on indefinitely.
choiceNotes: Correct. It drives the high side with the voltage stored on a capacitor.
A current mirror produces copies of a current.
A sample-and-hold temporarily holds a voltage.

power-050.question: In Baliga's figure of merit, used to compare materials for unipolar power devices, which material property has a particularly strong effect?
choices: Breakdown field (it enters as the cube)
power-050.explanation: Baliga's figure of merit, εμEc³ (permittivity, mobility and breakdown field), indicates how low a drift-layer resistance can be for a given voltage rating—higher is better. With the breakdown field cubed, SiC and GaN, whose Ec is about ten times silicon's, score hundreds of times higher even with similar or lower mobility. This is also why Ga2O3 and diamond, with even larger Ec, are promising next-generation materials.
choiceNotes: The lattice constant is not part of Baliga's figure of merit.
Correct. The breakdown field enters as the cube.
The thermal expansion coefficient is not part of Baliga's figure of merit.
